title: Third-party Inference Service SLA Negotiation Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic negotiation cheat sheet for commercial teams, legal, and security when contracting third-party inference services (hosted inference, model-hosting, managed endpoints). Focus: SLAs and measurable obligations that matter to production apps (latency P99, throughput, model availability, fallback behavior, telemetry needed for measurement, credits/offsets).

Audience and use:
- For deal: attach to commercial SOW or use as internal redline playbook.
- For SRE/infra: use as checklist to validate monitoring and test harness.
- For legal: suggested redlines and fallbacks.

High-level negotiation goals (ranked):
1) Measurable SLOs with clear measurement method (not fuzzy language).
2) Practical remediation (credits + runbook + rollback options) rather than unenforceable promises.
3) Observable telemetry and sampling windows so Redwood can independently verify compliance.
4) Defined fallbacks for degraded model/region capacity (model variant, regional failover, cached responses).
5) Data handling assurances aligned with DPA (no long-term retention of prompt content, ephemeral caches).

Core SLA clauses to push for (plain-language + suggested phrasing):
- Availability (control-plane + inference-plane):
  - "Inference Endpoint Availability: 99.95% monthly for inference requests measured at the region-level (inference-plane). Availability measured as successful 200-level responses within Xs of request arrival (see measurement)."
  - "Control Plane: 99.9% for configuration API and model rollout operations."
  - Rationale: ensure both runtime and management surfaces are covered.

- Latency SLOs (tail metrics matter):
  - Suggested: "P50/P90/P99 token generation latency windows per supported model class (e.g., 1–2B, 7–13B, 70B). Example: P99 < 600ms for short prompt (<=128 tokens) for model class M1 when not in cold-start."
  - Include cold-start definition and cold-start exclusion windows.
  - If vendor resists absolute numbers, accept relative baseline + regression guarantees (e.g., no >2x regression vs baseline within first 12 months).

- Throughput and concurrency guarantees:
  - "Committed throughput: X requests/minute sustained with spikes to Y for up to Z minutes per hour. Contention policy: vendor will prioritize committed capacity for Redwood account or implement graceful queuing with max wait time T."
  - Push for per-tenant isolation guarantees if using multi-tenant pools (or documented noisy-neighbor mitigations).

- Model availability & versioning:
  - "Model pinned versions: Redwood may pin a model version for production routes. Vendor will provide X days notice before model weight changes that could impact behavior and allow rollback to pinned version for Y days post-change."
  - Ask for a documented compatibility matrix for variant fallbacks (quantized vs full-precision) and expected output deviation bounds.

- Fallback and graceful degradation obligations:
  - "If primary model/region is unavailable, vendor will route to an approved fallback model or region. Vendor must send automated notifications and provide request-level indicators when a fallback was used."
  - Require an SLA for fallback success rate during incidents (e.g., 95% of requests should complete on fallback within T latency).

- Measurement & metrics (non-negotiable):
  - Measurement source: vendor should publish raw aggregated metrics via secure telemetry endpoints (per-tenant, time-windowed) and allow Redwood to corroborate with sampled request traces (redacted as needed).
  - Minimum metrics: request counts, success/error categories, latency histograms (P50/90/99), cold-start events, queue times, model_id used, region, fallback flag, sample of request IDs for post-incident triage.
  - Sampling: contract should specify sample fraction for request traces and maximum retention window.

- Credits, remedies, and termination triggers:
  - Financial credits: tiered schedule tied to severity and recurrence (example: <99.9% month -> 10% monthly service credit; <99.0% -> 30%). Require maximum credit cap AND right to terminate for repeated breaches (e.g., 3 successive months below 99.5%).
  - Performance regression escape hatch: if a model change causes material quality regression (measurable by Redwood-supplied eval suite), vendor must rollback within N days or issue credits and reimburse remediation costs for failed rollouts.

- Security and data handling intersection with DPA:
  - Ensure SLA references DPA obligations: ephemeral KV caches, no retention of raw prompts beyond stated window, audit logs on access to customer data, and KMS usage.
  - Require evidence hooks: vendor must provide attestation artifacts and redacted logs (within legal limits) to validate data-retention claims on request.

- Incident management and communication:
  - Response times: P1 incident acknowledgement < 15 minutes, mitigation/update cadence every 30–60 minutes until resolution.
  - Post-mortem: vendor to produce a post-incident report within 72 hours for P1/P2 with root cause, remediation plan, and corrective action timeline.

- Testing and ramp windows (important for rollouts):
  - Canary policy: vendor to support canary traffic weights and provide metric diffs between canary and baseline. Leave rollback guardrail in contract: immediate rollback if canary shows >X% increase in error rate or >Y% latency regression.

Language and definitional guidance (to avoid later disputes):
- Define measurement window: monthly rolling period unless otherwise stated.
- Define "unavailability" precisely: unsuccessful responses, internal errors, or responses exceeding agreed timeout.
- Define "cold start" (e.g., instance spin-up > 5 minutes after idle).

Negotiation levers and trade-offs (practical tactics):
- If vendor resists strict latency numbers: accept broader ranges + strong transparency (higher telemetry + shared benchmark runs).
- If vendor resists pinned model versions: require a guaranteed rollback path and a testing window before automatic model upgrades.
- Use committed spend to buy higher isolation and stronger SLOs (e.g., reserved capacity -> per-tenant pools).
- Prioritize predictable outage behavior over perfect uptime (i.e., documented fallbacks and SLOs for degraded mode).

Common vendor pushbacks and counter-positions (scripted responses):
- Vendor: "We can’t guarantee P99 for every model class."  Counter: "We accept class-level baselines + regression caps and must be able to run our eval suite post-change; credits if regression is material."
- Vendor: "We don’t disclose raw traces."  Counter: "We require sampled, redacted traces for verification; vendor can mask PII but must preserve request identifiers for correlation."

Evidence & acceptance criteria for go-live:
- Benchmarks: vendor to run agreed load test (X QPS across model classes) and share raw metrics.
- Observability: Redwood must be able to access vendor metrics API and get daily telemetry during first 90 days of production.
- Security: vendor completes onboarding checklist (SEC-ONB-2025) and provides penetration test report within 6 months.

Open questions / TODOs (internal):
- Finalize precise latency numbers per model class with benchmarks (action: infra to run profiling JIRA:INFRA-3421).
- Decide on maximum acceptable credit cap and termination thresholds (action: finance + legal).
- Confirm sampling retention limits compatible with privacy (action: privacy counsel).

Negotiation redlines (legal):
- No vague "commercially reasonable efforts" for latency or availability; must be quantifiable or excluded.
- Require audit rights for access to redacted telemetry in case of recurring disputes.
- Termination right after repeated SLA failures (3 months out-of-compliance) and refund pro rata of reserved fees for impacted period.

Quick checklist for commercial/solutions engineers when preparing an RFP or SOW:
- [ ] Include pinned model version clause and change-notice window.
- [ ] Define latency/availability measurement method and endpoints for telemetry.
- [ ] Demand per-tenant throughput isolation or documented mix and noisy-neighbor mitigations.
- [ ] Insist on sampled request traces (redacted) and latency histograms per region/model.
- [ ] Include fallback and routing commitments with notification mechanism.
- [ ] Outline financial credits and termination triggers for repeated breaches.
- [ ] Attach Redwood canonical eval suite and acceptance criteria.

Appendix: Example short-form SLA snippet to propose (editable):
"Vendor will provide Inference Endpoint Availability of 99.95% per calendar month for all production endpoints, measured by successful inference responses within a 3 second application-level timeout. Availability excludes: scheduled maintenance (48 hours prior notice), force majeure, and Redwood-initiated configuration changes. If monthly availability falls below 99.95%, Vendor will apply service credits as follows: [99.0%–99.95%: 10% credit; 98.0%–99.0%: 25% credit; <98.0%: 50% credit] and Redwood may terminate the Agreement after three consecutive months below 99.5%. Vendor will publish per-tenant latency histograms (P50/P90/P99) and provide sampled redacted traces at a minimum sampling rate of 0.1% for the first 90 days of production and 0.01% thereafter."

Notes to self: keep this doc conversational — sales likes bullet examples, legal likes precise definitions. Update after first vendor negotiation cycle (track outcomes).

History: created as consolidation of SRE/Legal/Commercial post-mortem from two vendor incidents in Q3–Q4 2025.

Contact: Maya Desai (legal) — for redlines and escalation.
